title: Orchestrated canary promotions with drift detection for private control plane upgrades
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Build an automated, safe promotion pipeline for control plane version upgrades in Private/VPC deployments that (1) detects configuration or version drift between desired state and deployed controlplanes, (2) orchestrates small canary cohorts using Terraform/IaC modules, and (3) promotes or rolls back based on telemetry and safety gates. This ticket covers the orchestrator glue, terraform module changes (version pinning and gradation knobs), telemetry thresholds, and a runbook for operators.
acceptance_criteria: A1: The orchestrator can target a named set of tenants (cohort) and apply a staged Terraform plan that upgrades controlplane version for only those tenants
A2: Drift detector produces a report highlighting mismatched controlplane binaries, CRD versions, and module configuration for >95% of tenants within 30 minutes of scan
A3: Canary cohort promotion automation will automatically advance to the next cohort when all defined SLO thresholds are met for a configurable observation window
A4: Automated rollback is triggered if any of the primary safety signals (controlplane API error rate, controller crashloop rate, or region-wide latency p50 regression) exceed configured thresholds
A5: Telemetry dashboards and alerting runbooks are created and linked; on-call can execute a manual abort that prevents further promotions
A6: End-to-end integration tests validate a simulated failed canary (introduce a deliberate config change) results in rollback and correct remediation actions
proposed_solution: 1) Drift detection: implement a periodic comparator that uses Terraform state snapshots + live API queries to detect divergence in controlplane version, CRD schemas, and module input diffs. Results stored as artifacts in S3 with a signed URL for engineers.

2) Terraform modules: add an explicit 'upgrade_channel' input and 'batch_token' output to existing private/controlplane module. Module will accept 'target_version' and 'preflight_checks' boolean. Produce human-readable plan summaries as metadata.

3) Orchestrator: extend existing upgrade-orchestrator service to accept cohorts, run 'terraform plan/apply' for targeted tenant workspaces, and gate promotion with safety policy engine (SPE) that evaluates telemetry queries.

4) Safety signals: define a small set of canary SLOs (controlplane API 5xx rate, controller restart count, reconciler latencies, host GPU contention). Implement short-term baselining and dynamic thresholds (delta-based) to reduce false positives.
5) Circuit breaker: if a safety signal trips, orchestrator immediately runs the module's rollback path and halts further cohorts. Events emitted to audit log and Slack #infra-upgrades channel.
6) Testing harness: introduce a 'chaos' mode in staging that can flip specific checks to false to validate rollback behavior in CI.
7) Docs & Runbook: operator-facing runbook with checklist, escalation matrix, and manual promote/abort commands for SREs and SEs.
8) Security: require a signed intent (two-person approval) for any promotion into cohorts that contain customers with 'regulated' label. Integrate KMS-signed promotion tokens.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Dry run (week 1): Run drift detector across all staging tenants, generate reports, and validate Terraform plan metadata generation (no applies).
Phase 1 - Canary (week 2): Run orchestrator against an internal-only tenant cohort (5 tenants). Observe 12h and 72h telemetry windows. Manual promotion only.
Phase 2 - Automated small cohort (week 3): Enable automated promotion for non-regulated tenants with cohort size 10 and 24h observation window. Monitor alerts closely.

Phase 3 - Broader roll (week 4+): Increase cohort sizes, add regulated tenants after security sign-off and two-person approval. Gradually tune promotion thresholds based on observed false-positive rate.
Fallback: Any circuit-breaker trip triggers immediate rollback and creates a postmortem ticket template.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from short-term noise cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: use delta-based baselines and require sustained breach over observation window before tripping.
Risk: Terraform state drift leads to inconsistent rollbacks. Mitigation: always snapshot state before apply, and verify plan matches snapshot; if mismatch, escalate to manual review.
Risk: Attack surface for automated promotion. Mitigation: require signed promotion tokens for regulated cohorts and audit all actions with immutable logs.
Risk: Insufficient test coverage for tenant-specific module inputs. Mitigation: add combinatorial unit tests for module inputs and a staging job that replays common tenant configs.
